quest.title: The Chasm Charters
quest.description: Lan of the Adventurers' Guild has offered you a commission to explore The Chasm, which you have accepted. First, you'll need to find the representative of the Ministry of Civil Affairs, Muning, who has been stationed there.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you. Well, are you here to brave The Chasm by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Chasm?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's never heard of any commission like that...

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Oh, uh, you don't know about the Guild's commissions yet? Sorry, that's my mistake.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Well, The Chasm has been closed for a long time now. No one can go in without the Qixing's say-so, not even the Adventurers' Guild.

choices.text: No special pass for you guys?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Well, we wouldn't dream of being a bother to the people at Yujing Terrace. It would be a counterproductive thing to do, messing with pre-established policy like that.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Even Ms. Ganyu, who seems like the most amicable of the bunch, would probably just smile at us and say "why don't you have some tea while you wait here?"

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: And then she'll leave you hanging for most of the day, until you start wondering whether she'd forgotten all about you till she was nearly off from work...

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Hmph, and as we all know, Ms. Ganyu never gets off work.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That certainly does sound like a very Ganyu-esque way of refusing.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Either way, this means that Ms. Katheryne isn't going to be giving out any commissions about The Chasm anytime soon. Instead, we've got to find more... convenient people to help us out in private.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Convenient?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Yes, like for example, miners from Huishan Hall, members of the Millelith, staff at the Ministry of Civil Affairs. They can get passes to go in more easily, and...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And... what?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Well... So what I'm saying is, O valiant hero who saved Liyue from the sea monster, yet seems to have nothing to do all day every day, surely you can talk to the Millelith on our behalf?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No idea who you're talking about.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I'm talking about you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, she was definitely talking about you!

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Don't play dumb. Who do you think I'm talking about, Rex Lapis?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Alright, quit your bragging.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Whatever the case... You have our thanks for your help so far, and we'd like you to consider helping us again.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: It's fine if the timing isn't convenient for you. It's just that... If you do end up passing through The Chasm, please help me look for a fellow named Muning.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Muning... Who's that supposed to be?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: He's a specialist sent to The Chasm by the Ministry of Civil Affairs. We've got some personal matters that need settling. You can ask him about it if you meet him there.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Just pass this message along: "You still owe Lan money for drinks. Don't you forget that." He'll get the picture.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Wait, hold on a moment! There's one more thing. If you take this commission up, just negotiate your payment directly with Muning.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Don't ask me why the arrangement is like this... We did this at the Ministry's insistence. Best not to question their decisions and all...

choices.text: I'll keep an eye out on the way in.
I'll have you know that I do some important work, you know.
They don't close one eye with you lot?

talks.objective: Search for Muning, the Ministry of Civil Affairs' specialist

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you tell me more about The Chasm?

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Right, so about the Chasm... If you don't intend to leave just yet, you're free to explore the area a bit. But please do keep your actions within the remit of Liyue's laws and statutes.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: I should mention, though, that there is a place that I highly recommend you avoid.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: For example, the great mine in the center of The Chasm has had a Seven-Star Array cast over it... By which I mean exactly what I say — it is a seal placed over the area by the Qixing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, that's quite the clear explanation.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: As for the weak... I mean, focal point of the array, it lies in the Bedrock Keys surrounding the area. These were placed by the Qixing themselves. Connected in series, they affix the energy flowing through the array.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: The area around the Bedrock Keys has seen an abnormal amount of Geo elemental coalescences. It's almost as if the "thing" beneath yearns to finally emerge...

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: ...Uh, never mind me, I was just talking to myself. So yes, that's how things are. Please do not — and I repeat, do not — go near the Seven-Star Array, and don't even think about going down there to explore.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: The Bedrock Keys are definitely not losing structural integrity, and the surrounding areas are most certainly not plagued by any strange Geo elemental convergences. So please, don't you think of doing anything at all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Hmph, I know what you're going to ask.

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: There are most certainly no precious treasures down there, nor are there any prehistoric fossils to be had. And banish any thoughts you have about giant ancient ruins... Yes, please do not bear any fruitless expectations toward this place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The way you're saying all this is super suspicious!

dialogues.speaker: Muning
dialogues.text: Not even mushrooms will grow down there! Nor are there wish-granting stones! And there are definitely no sailors who grow strong just by eating mushrooms! Again, do not get your hopes up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, yeah, sure! There's no need to be so fierce...

choices.text: Anything else I should look out for?

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: I suggest that you go speak to Zhiqiong first. She is an adventurer hired by the Ministry and was once a miner here. She knows The Chasm's geography like the back of her hand...

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Also, let me write you a certification real quick. When she sees it, she'll know that you're trustworthy.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: That said, I must warn you that Zhiqiong is definitely not the sort of person who has trouble standing still, and definitely has no thoughts of undoing the array and having a look underground.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: So there's no way that she would ever put a team of idle adventurers together to brazenly enter hazardous areas! As such, you can forget about asking her to help you enter The Chasm's mines.

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Did... did you really?

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: As long as you understand, we're good, in which case, I won't take up any more of your time.

choices.text: Got it, then. Come, Paimon, let's go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, let's go!

response.speaker: Muning
response.text: Wait! I haven't finished!

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: You're back. The Adventurers' Guild welcomes you.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: What, you want me to tell you what's in there? Who knows, seriously?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Some say that the some miners dug up what they call "Wish Granter," but that they got the opposite of what they wished for when they wished upon it. Others say that they dug up some old dragon-king's tail down there. All tales as tall as mountains, of course.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Really, there's no point asking me about The Chasm. I'm not actually sure what happened there either. Just go ask Muning — this was also one of the Ministry's requirements, by the way.

choices.text: Tell me more about the commission...

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: *cough* Well, you can see the people who depend on The Chasm for their livelihood everywhere you go out there. I'm sure you don't mind spending time interviewing them, but I've got Guild business to attend to.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Oh, him? Heh. I suspect that the Ministry sent him out to The Chasm to get him to shape up a bit.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: He's pretty good at what he does, alright, but he's one cocky kid as well. You can't have that kind of flighty character in the Ministry, you know? So yeah. The Chasm might help him grow up a bit.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Yeah, sure. Oh, right... Ad astra abyssosque!
